---
title: "Batch downloads"
toc: true
---

`Fetcher(..., batch_days=7)` groups retrieval work into windows of up to seven
UTC calendar days. Daily sources still produce their usual daily files. Omitting
the option (`batch_days=None`) keeps the existing behavior.

```python
import collekt

config = collekt.DatasetConfig(
    collekt.ERA5("era5_reanalysis", variables=["10m_u_component_of_wind", "10m_v_component_of_wind"]),
)
request = collekt.Request(
    region=collekt.Region.from_bbox((4.75, 8.25, 39.75, 42.75)),
    start="2022-11-01",
    end="2022-11-07",
)
fetcher = collekt.Fetcher(
    request=request,
    config=config,
    output_dir="data/collections",
    batch_days=7,
)
plan = fetcher.plan()       # inspect retrieval groups before downloading
result = fetcher.download()
```

For this complete, uncached ERA5 week, one CDS retrieval produces seven daily
NetCDF files. Their filenames, variable attributes, coordinates, native hourly
sampling, and per-day temporal metadata follow the existing output contract.
`Assembler` works with them in the same way as with daily downloads.

## Choosing a size

`batch_days` accepts a positive Python integer. Booleans, zero, negative values,
fractions, and duration strings such as `"7d"` or `"48h"` are rejected. Use
`batch_days=2` for two UTC calendar days. This setting controls retrieval windows;
it does not multiply the dataset's sampling interval.

Windows begin on the first requested UTC date and are clipped to the original
request. Provider constraints, cache gaps, and incompatible selections can split
a window further. `batch_days=1` enables the batch machinery with one-day groups;
it is distinct from the default `None`, since event sources normally query the
whole collection at once.

There is no universal best size. Larger requests reduce per-request overhead but
can increase provider queue time, memory use, and the work repeated after a
failure. Provider volume limits still apply; collekt does not automatically retry
an oversized batch as smaller batches. Event APIs that already accept the whole
request may need **more** calls when explicit windows are enabled.

## Behavior by source

| Source | Retrieval with `batch_days` | Output |
|---|---|---|
| ERA5 | One CDS request per compatible group. Groups stay within one year/month and share the same hour selection. Partial first/last days can form smaller groups. Requires unarchived NetCDF. | Original daily NetCDF files. |
| CMEMS | Multi-day `subset` calls for `outside` and `nearest` coordinate selection. Daily slices reproduce the Toolbox's selection, including boundary neighbours. `inside` and `strict-inside` retain daily calls because their empty-selection fallback needs the provider's full time index. | Original daily NetCDF files. |
| ECMWF Open Data | One client call for compatible forecast dates/steps. The SDK may still download multiple remote files. Splitting uses forecast run time and retains lead times and valid times. | Original file per forecast run/day. |
| GFS | Logical groups of analysis cycles; each native cycle still has its own URL and transfer. | Original daily NetCDF files. |
| eOdyn | Logical groups of the existing daily archive reads. The production API remains unavailable. | Original daily NetCDF files. |
| Local | Consecutive days sharing the same archive files can be read together, then partitioned by UTC day. Different archive file sets start new groups. | Original daily annotated Parquet files. |
| SkyTruth | Paginated queries for each window; duplicate feature IDs are removed across windows. | One annotated Parquet file for the collection. |
| Global Fishing Watch | Paginated queries for each window; duplicate event IDs are removed, events are sorted by start time, and `max_events` caps the combined result with a truncation warning. | One annotated Parquet file for the collection. |
| HOZINT | One isolated CLI invocation per window, with a completion marker for reliable retries. | CLI-generated Parquet files under `batches/<id>/` within the source directory. |
| Copernicus Data Space | Date-window searches with pagination and product deduplication. `max_records` caps unique catalogue records across all windows. Each product still downloads separately. | Original product filenames. |

SkyTruth and Data Space query windows overlap at midnight to avoid dropping
fractional-second timestamps when serializing inclusive endpoints. Records with
the same provider identifier are emitted once. GFW uses its native exclusive end
date convention. For Data Space, a dry run lists all candidate searches; execution
stops early if `max_records` is reached.

## Cache, failures, and metadata

Collection directories remain keyed by the original region and time range.
Existing daily files are reused, including files from a non-batched run. Only
missing consecutive days are grouped. Changing `batch_days` does not invalidate
completed daily files. As before, cache reuse assumes that files at their expected
paths are complete; it is not a content-integrity check.

New grid slices and assembled event/local files are written to temporary files
and published after successful writing. Failed grid batches do not prevent later
batches from running. A missing ERA5 timestamp prevents that daily slice from
being treated as complete. Event queries checkpoint completed windows; if another
window fails, no partial collection file is published, and the next run can reuse
the completed queries. Data Space also caches completed searches. These checkpoints
live inside the collection directory; `download(use_cache=False)` ignores them.

HOZINT stores each window separately so a file from the first window cannot make
later windows appear cached. A failed CLI invocation's temporary output is
discarded. Existing output from a non-batched HOZINT run has no window completion
markers and is therefore not used as a batch cache.

Per-file `details.batch`, or `details.batches` for an assembled event file,
records the retrieval IDs, bounds, transport type, and provider parameters.
Cached files retain their recorded retrieval provenance even if a subsequent run
changes the batch size or returns to default downloading. Summary counters remain
**file/result counts**, not network-request counts. See [Manifest](manifest.qmd).

Provider history and job metadata describe the batch that produced the data.
Standard `time_coverage_start`, `time_coverage_end`, and `time_coverage_duration`
attributes, when present, are narrowed to each daily grid slice. Other provider
attributes are retained; bespoke provider attributes are not interpreted.

## Small ERA5 benchmark

A live benchmark on 22 September 2026 compared sequential daily CDS requests
with batches over the same small western Mediterranean area. It requested both
10 m wind components, all 24 hours, unarchived NetCDF, over dates in November 2022.
Two three-day comparisons reversed the order of daily and batch runs:

| Comparison | Three daily downloads | One batch, including daily splitting |
|---|---:|---:|
| Daily first (14–16 November) | 91.79 s | 119.33 s |
| Batch first (21–23 November) | 146.98 s | 56.93 s |
| Combined | 238.77 s | 176.26 s |

The combined batch time was **26.2% lower**, but one trial was slower because of
the CDS queue. Total server processing in the matched trials fell from 79.32 s
to 29.92 s. Daily data values, coordinates, dimensions, and variable attributes
matched after splitting.

An additional ten-day batch took **119.20 s**, including **0.494 s** to split the
daily files. There was no matched ten-day daily baseline and no 150-day request.
These small measurements support making batching optional; they do not establish
a dependable speedup for larger regions or long periods. Provider caching was
not disabled. Nine jobs transferred approximately 0.82 MB in total.

The benchmark used cdsapi 0.7.7, ecmwf-datastores-client 0.5.3, and xarray
2026.7.0, with CDS area `[42.75, 4.75, 39.75, 8.25]` (north, west, south, east).
Provider queue and polling delays make elapsed time variable even when the
retrieval work is identical.
